lead: A radar sees strong echoes from ground, sea, buildings and rain. These echoes are clutter. Clutter can hide an aircraft because it is much stronger and has no Doppler shift. MTI and pulse Doppler radar solve this by comparing successive pulses and cancelling anything stationary. The delay-line canceller gives zeros at Doppler frequencies called blind speeds, fixed by wavelength and PRF. Pulse Doppler radar adds a bank of Doppler filters, so it can also measure velocity. These ideas are used in airport surveillance, weather radar and fighter fire control.
prereq: You need: the Doppler shift from 6.5, and PRF and range gating from 6.4.

blocks.text: An echo from ground, sea, buildings or rain is called clutter. Clutter can be 40–60 dB stronger than an aircraft echo. A fixed threshold high enough to reject clutter also rejects the aircraft. The Doppler shift separates them. A target with radial velocity vr gives fd = 2vr/λ, where λ is the wavelength and fd the Doppler frequency in hertz. Stationary clutter has fd = 0. MTI stores the video of one pulse, compares it with the next pulse, and subtracts. Any echo with the same phase cancels. A moving target changes phase, so a residue remains. The subtraction is done separately in each range bin: the sample at delay 2R/c is kept and cancelled bin by bin. This is range gating. Coherent MTI uses a stable transmitted phase reference; noncoherent MTI uses echo amplitude changes and suits magnetron transmitters.
A single delay-line canceller subtracts the previous pulse from the present pulse after a delay Tr. Tr is the pulse repetition time in seconds. Its transfer function magnitude is

blocks.where: H(fd) is the voltage response at Doppler frequency fd in Hz; Tr is the pulse repetition time in s.

blocks.text: The response is zero when fd = n/Tr = n PRF, with n = 0, 1, 2, ... and PRF the pulse repetition frequency in hertz. Those Doppler frequencies are blind speeds. In terms of target speed,

blocks.where: vb is the blind radial speed in m/s; λ is the wavelength in m; PRF is in Hz; n = 1, 2, 3, ...

blocks.text: The response peaks at odd multiples of PRF/2 with value 2. A double canceller cascades two single cancellers. Its magnitude is |H| = 4 sin²(π fd Tr). The notch around each zero is wider, so slow clutter is rejected better, but low-Doppler targets lose more signal and phase errors hurt more. Improvement factor I is the output signal-to-clutter ratio divided by the input signal-to-clutter ratio, usually in dB. Staggered PRF changes the PRF pulse to pulse, so the zeros move and no single speed is blind all the time; the price is range-ambiguity bookkeeping.

Pulse Doppler radar sends many pulses per dwell and passes each range bin through a bank of Doppler filters. Each filter covers a Doppler band. The output is a range-Doppler map. The filter with the largest output gives the target velocity; a longer dwell gives finer velocity resolution. Platform motion spreads the clutter spectrum, so airborne and spaceborne radars need clutter compensation. MTD, the moving target detector, is a practical combination: a canceller followed by a small Doppler filter bank, common in airport surveillance. Coherent MTI uses the transmitter phase reference; noncoherent MTI uses amplitude only and works with magnetron transmitters. Uses include airport surveillance, weather Doppler radar for rain motion, and fighter fire control.

items: MTI removes stationary clutter; it does not measure velocity.
Pulse Doppler measures velocity by which filter is strongest.
Blind speeds come from Doppler nulls; range ambiguities come from PRF.

spec.aria: Response of a single delay-line canceller with a 1 ms repetition period: zeros at 0, 1000 and 2000 Hz which are the blind Doppler frequencies, and peaks of value two in between.

examples.question: An X-band MTI radar has wavelength λ = 3 cm and PRF = 1000 Hz. Find the first two blind speeds in m/s and in km/h.
steps: The pulse repetition time is Tr = 1/PRF = 1/1000 s = 1 ms.
Blind speed formula: vb = n λ PRF / 2.
examples.answer: The first two blind speeds are 15 m/s (54 km/h) and 30 m/s (108 km/h).

lam = 0.03
prf = 1000.0

traps: Saying MTI measures velocity. A canceller only removes stationary clutter; velocity comes from a Doppler filter bank.
Confusing blind speed with maximum unambiguous range. Blind speed comes from fd = n PRF; range ambiguity comes from the wait time between pulses.
Putting λ in centimetres into vb = n λ PRF / 2 without converting to metres.
Assuming a double canceller is always better. It has a wider notch but more loss and more sensitivity to phase errors.
Forgetting that staggered PRF trades blind speeds for range-ambiguity bookkeeping.

quiz.q: A single delay-line canceller has Tr = 0.5 ms. At what Doppler frequencies does its response fall to zero?
quiz.a: fd = n/Tr = n × 2000 Hz, for n = 0, 1, 2, ... So the zeros are at 0, 2000, 4000 Hz, ...

quiz.q: Why does a simple amplitude threshold fail against ground clutter?
quiz.a: Ground clutter can be much stronger than the target echo and has no Doppler shift. A threshold high enough to reject clutter also rejects the weaker moving target. MTI subtracts the stationary echoes before detection.

quiz.q: An MTI radar has λ = 0.1 m and PRF = 500 Hz. Find the first blind speed.
Why does a double canceller have a wider blind-speed notch but is not always preferred?
quiz.a: The wider notch rejects slow clutter better than a single canceller. It also attenuates low-Doppler target echoes more, needs more delay hardware and is more sensitive to phase errors between pulses.

quiz.q: What is the improvement factor of an MTI radar?
quiz.a: It is the output signal-to-clutter ratio divided by the input signal-to-clutter ratio, usually expressed in dB.

quiz.q: An X-band radar has λ = 3 cm and PRF = 2000 Hz. Find the first blind speed.
How does staggered PRF remove blind speeds, and what price is paid?
quiz.a: Changing Tr pulse to pulse moves the Doppler nulls, so no fixed target speed is blind on every pulse. The price is extra range-ambiguity bookkeeping and more complex clutter suppression.

quiz.q: What is range gating in MTI?
quiz.a: The receiver keeps the video sample belonging to one range delay, 2R/c, and performs the pulse-to-pulse cancellation separately for each range bin. Targets at different ranges are thus processed in separate bins.

beyond: Not for the exam. Modern radars use space-time adaptive processing (STAP) on phased arrays to suppress clutter while keeping moving-target detection. Ground moving-target indication (GMTI) in airborne radar is a direct descendant. Weather Doppler radars often use pulse-pair processing rather than display cancellers. Search terms: STAP, GMTI, pulse-Doppler filter bank, staggered PRF.
